overview: Atlantis is the city of the fourteen poems. It is a harbour city that kept its flood, a city reversed out of 2,707 pictures, built and broken and repaired across six eras. It lives by the tide, not the clock. It remembers the Fall in a salt line at four metres on every old wall. It mends its ruins in white ceramic seamed with light. And it keeps every frame it was made from on a hill, turning, where everyone can read it. Meaning here is use: the same stones have been a harbour, a dock, a ruin and a club.

calendar.name: The day of two gates
calendar.text: Atlantis does not keep a twenty-four-hour day. A day is two risings of the Tide Engine's gates, roughly every 12 hours 25 minutes, so the day drifts against the sun and a market can fall at dawn one month and at dusk the next. Appointments are made 'at the second gate' or 'between gates'.

calendar.name: First Tide
calendar.text: The year begins on the first spring tide after the equinox. The avenue walks through the Light Gate toward the sea. The Salt Guild carries cups of seawater up the Salt Stair to the Archive, so the hill will remember the bay. The Keepers re-order the Archive's panels that night.

calendar.name: The Night of the Line
calendar.text: On the anniversary of the Fall, people chalk the flood line on every wall that does not already carry it: new houses, glass towers, the white temple. For one night the whole city stands at the same height of water. In the morning the rain takes the chalk.

calendar.name: Relighting
calendar.text: The Resurrection is kept at midwinter, when the warehouses on the old docks were first relit as clubs. Every neon band in the nightlife district is switched on at once, and the Resonator's pulse is timed to the first chord.

institutions.name: the Tide Office
institutions.text: It keeps the gates, the tables and the time. It is the oldest office in the city and the only one whose clerks are allowed to be late; they answer to the water. Its notices are posted at every pier: the next two gates and the height of each.

institutions.name: the Keepers
institutions.text: They keep the Archive. They hold that the city is a way of arranging its pictures and that rearranging them is civic work. A Keeper's training is to look at one frame for a whole tide. They are the only people who can say which panel is which without counting.

institutions.name: the Resonance Society
institutions.text: They tune the pipes on the summit and argue about the note. One faction wants the pulse to follow the tide exactly; another wants it to follow the poems, one line per gate. For now the tide wins.

institutions.name: the Avenue Wardens
institutions.text: They keep the processional avenue from the pyramids to the Light Gate. They are a ceremonial body with one practical duty: lighting the lamps on the Salt Stair.

institutions.name: the Salt Guild
institutions.text: The salt carriers built the first street, which is a stair. The guild still owns the harbour's white trade: salt, the ceramic that repairs the ruins, and the right to sell seawater on First Tide.

institutions.name: the Glaziers
institutions.text: The white trade's craftsmen. They fit the ceramic plates over the ruined brick and draw the cyan seam. Any house can ask for a plate, but the seam has to be drawn by a Glazier, and no two are drawn alike.

institutions.name: the Boroughs Council
institutions.text: The city's government, elected by ward (the wards are the voting districts on the map). It built the Skywalk, the maglev and the evolved towers, and it is argued with in every café.

institutions.name: the Ferrymen
institutions.text: They run the skiffs between the towers' crowns and the maglev on its pylons. The name is older than the machines; they ran boats across the flooded streets in the season after the Fall.

trades.name: the white trade
trades.text: Salt, glazed ceramic and the repair of ruins. The city's richest and oldest industry, and the one you can see from anywhere: every white plate on a brick wall is a Glazier's bill paid.

trades.name: sugar
trades.text: The refinery on the waterfront still burns its red SUGAR sign over the harbour. Its silos are the tallest things on the port side, and on a warm night the whole district smells of it.

trades.name: tide power
trades.text: The Tide Engine's turbines run the maglev and the Archive's drums. When the gates rise, the city's lights brighten for a minute. People call that minute the hot minute, after the poem.

trades.name: pictures
trades.text: The Archive sells nothing, but the city trades in frames. A panel moved to the outside of a drum is worth something to whoever is in it, and footage of a neighbourhood decides where the Council builds.

transit.name: the Cyan Line
transit.text: The maglev, on white pylons twenty-six metres up, runs between the evolved towers on a minimum spanning line. Each car has warm windows; at night the line is a slow string of light over the roofs.

transit.name: the skiffs
transit.text: Small craft fly lanes between the crowns of the towers, run by the Ferrymen. They cannot land in the old town; the Wardens forbid it.

transit.name: the bus
transit.text: Bus stops every few hundred metres on the arterials. They came in the New Boroughs era. The shelters are the most common thing in the archive after puddles.

transit.name: the Salt Stair
transit.text: Still the shortest way from the harbour to the hill, and still walked.

customs.name: Where do you go?
customs.text: The city's greeting. The answer is 'when I leave', from the title of the album. Saying anything else marks a visitor.

customs.name: Stairs are streets
customs.text: Addresses on the hill are given by flight and landing, not by number: 'the third landing of the Salt Stair, the door with the blue plate'.

customs.name: Meaning is use
customs.text: A building's name is what it is used for now. The warehouse is 'the club'. The chapel's ruin under the vault is 'the white temple'. The ruin field is 'the walk'. Old names survive only in the Archive.

customs.name: Never repair the line
customs.text: You may plate a ruin, add a floor or relight a warehouse, but you do not paint over the flood line. A clean wall at four metres is a lie about the city.

customs.name: The pulse
customs.text: When the cyan ring crosses the facades at night, people on the street stop talking until it has passed.

sayings: two gates and a hot minute
it's under the line (it is old)
a Keeper's look (a very long stare)
the bay keeps it (it is lost and that is fine)
